### 1. Your facts, played back plainly

You are 30. You work now as a Retail Sales Associate. You earn about $38K a year.

You said the minimum pay you need is $40K a year.

Here is what you have to work with: - 4 hours a day for training or a switch - $20K budget - 12 months of cushion - Your documents are in order - No health limits you named

You have started 3 serious things and finished 2 of them. Money running out is what stopped you before.

Your top must-have at work is Relationships. Your second is Support.

Some of your answers were still thin, so your scores below are ranges, not single numbers. The direction is still clear. The picks are from different worlds — healthcare, working with people, and business — not three versions of the same job.

### 2. What shapes what is honestly possible

Your cushion and budget cover the shorter roads in. Your 4 hours a day set the pace.

Money is the barrier to watch. It stopped you before, so any plan has to keep income running while you switch. For all three picks below, the advice in your results is the same: keep Retail Sales Associate paying while you switch. Do not quit first.

You ranked Relationships #1 and Support #2. A job that is weak on either one will rub, even if the pay looks fine. That shows up in the picks below.

### 3. The top candidates

**1. Doula — Top fit** - LOVE 0.83–1.00 - POTENTIAL 0.74–1.00

Why this fits: Your #1 must-have is Relationships, and this job delivers it. Your #2 must-have is Support, and this job delivers that too.

The numbers: Typical pay is about $45K a year. Your minimum is $40K, so typical pay clears it. Time to get in is about 3.5 months of training. There is no checked data on AI risk for this job yet, so no number is invented here.

This is the cleanest fit of the three on what you ranked highest. Both of your top two must-haves are met, not just one.

**2. Private Tutor (in person) — Top fit** - LOVE 0.79–1.00 - POTENTIAL 0.77–1.00

Why this fits: Your #1 must-have is Relationships, and this job delivers it.

The numbers: Typical pay is about $45K a year. Your minimum is $40K, so typical pay clears it. Time to get in is about 3.5 months of training. There is no checked data on AI risk for this job yet, so no number is invented here.

The strain is clear, too. You ranked Support #2, and this job is weak exactly there. That is friction you would feel every week.

**3. Tutoring Center Owner — Top fit** - LOVE 0.79–1.00 - POTENTIAL 0.77–1.00

Why this fits: Your #1 must-have is Relationships, and this job delivers it.

The numbers: Typical pay is about $75K a year. Your minimum is $40K, so typical pay clears it. Time to get in is about 9 months of training — much longer than the other two. There is no checked data on AI risk for this job yet, so no number is invented here.

The strain is the same as with tutoring on your own. You ranked Support #2, and this job is weak exactly there. That is friction you would feel every week. The longer road in also means more months to fund before it pays.

### Your cushion

Your main road pays later, so Community Health Worker carries the bills meanwhile — it is the floor under the main road, not a second verdict and not a better match. LOVE 0.78–1.00, POTENTIAL 0.77–1.00. It has a short road in, about 3.5 months of training before employers hire, and it is licensed work — employers hire for the license, which keeps the seat stable. It also feeds your main road: both this job and Doula are people-facing work, so the muscle transfers. Typical pay is about $51K a year, which clears your $40K minimum from the first paycheck.

### 4. The honest BUT

For Doula: Money running out is what stopped you before. This path has to be paced so it does not happen again. Keep your current job paying while you train.

For Private Tutor (in person): Same money warning. Also, the Support gap is real. You ranked Support #2, and this job is weak there. People usually quit paths like this not because the work is wrong on day one, but because that weekly friction builds up.

For Tutoring Center Owner: Same money warning, and same Support gap. Plus, 9 months of training is a long stretch at 4 hours a day. That is where people usually quit — in the middle months, before any pay from the new road starts.

Pay check on all three: Each one clears your $40K minimum on typical pay. Doula is about $45K, Private Tutor (in person) is about $45K, and Tutoring Center Owner is about $75K. None of these is being presented as working only at a top-earner tier, and none misses your floor on typical pay. The risk is not the final pay. The risk is the months before that pay starts.

### 5. Jobs to run from

Knowing what to run from is half the match. This is protection, not failure. The matchmaker does not let you marry the wrong career.

**1. Data Center Technician** — Worst fit of the three. You put Relationships at #1 and Support at #2, and this job gives you very little of either. The daily setup fights how you work best, so you would be forcing yourself every day. Typical pay is about $72K and clears your $40K minimum, but pay does not fix a daily fit this wrong.

**2. Vertical Farm Technician** — You put Relationships at #1 and Support at #2, and this job gives you very little of either. The daily setup fights how you work best, every day. Typical pay is about $48K and clears your $40K minimum, but the fit problem stays.

**3. Medical Laboratory Scientist** — You put Relationships at #1 and Support at #2, and this job gives you very little of either, and the daily setup fights how you work best. It also takes about 36 months of training before it pays anything. Your cushion is 12 months, so the money runs out first. Typical pay is about $63K and clears your $40K minimum, but you would not reach that pay before the cushion ends.

### 6. The 90-day check plan

**Days 1–7:** Pick the one of the top three you would try first. Before you spend a dollar on it, do one real task from that job — a trial day or a sample project. Keep your Retail Sales Associate job paying.

**Days 8–30:** Start the first training steps for your pick at your 4-hours-a-day pace. For Doula or Private Tutor (in person), that road is about 3.5 months total. For Tutoring Center Owner, it is about 9 months, so by day 30 you should know if that longer pace still feels doable.

**Days 31–60:** Keep training. Check your money once a week against your 12-month cushion and $20K budget. If spending is running ahead of plan, slow the spending, not your current income.

**Days 61–90:** Do another real task from the job, bigger than the first one. Ask yourself two plain questions: Does this work give me the Relationships I ranked #1? And, for the tutor picks, is the weak Support already bothering me every week?

**By the 90-day check-in, you will know:** whether you finished the first real tasks, whether the training pace at 4 hours a day is holding, whether your money is still on track, and whether the Support gap — if your pick has one — is a small rub or a weekly problem.

Your one next step this week: choose Doula, Private Tutor (in person), or Tutoring Center Owner as your first try, and book one trial day or sample project for it before you spend anything on training.
